question.:question/problem:
Find $m,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=k(x)$ at the point where $x=0.$

We have $k(x)=-x^{3} -x + 2 e^{x}$ and $k^{\prime}(x)=-3 x^{2} + 2 e^{x} -1.$

$m=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have $k(x)=-x^{3} -x + 2 e^{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is equal to $k^{\prime}(0).$ The given derivative is

$$
k^{\prime}(x)=-3 x^{2} + 2 e^{x} -1.
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=0$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}k^{\prime}(0) & =-3 (0)^{2} + 2 e^{(0)} -1 \\ & =-1+0+2 \\ & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $1.$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=x^{7} -4 x^{5} -136 x$ at the point where $x=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^{7} -4 x^{5} -136 x.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x^{7} -4 x^{5} -136 x) \\ & =7 x^{6} -20 x^{4} -136.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(2) & =7 (2)^{6} -20 (2)^{4} -136 \\ & =-136-320+448 \\ & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $-8.$

Let $f(x)=x^{7} -7 x^{5} -2261 x.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(3).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x^{7} -7 x^{5} -2261 x) \\ & =7 x^{6} -35 x^{4} -2261.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(3) & =7 (3)^{6} -35 (3)^{4} -2261 \\ & =-2261-2835+5103 \\ & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $7.$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=2 x^{7} -6 x^{5} -7773 x$ at the point where $x=3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{7} -6 x^{5} -7773 x.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(3).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2 x^{7} -6 x^{5} -7773 x) \\ & =14 x^{6} -30 x^{4} -7773.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(3) & =14 (3)^{6} -30 (3)^{4} -7773 \\ & =-7773-2430+10206 \\ & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $3.$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=3 x^{4} -5 x^{3} + \frac{1}{x}$ at the point where $x=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=3 x^{4} -5 x^{3} + \frac{1}{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3 x^{4} -5 x^{3} + \frac{1}{x}) \\ & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3 x^{4} -5 x^{3}+x^{-1}) \\ & =4\cdot3x^{3}-3\cdot5x^{2}-x^{-2} \\ & =12 x^{3} -15 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(2) & =12 (2)^{3} -15 (2)^{2} -\frac{1}{(2)^{2}} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}-60+96 \\ & =\frac{143}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $\frac{143}{4}.$

Let $f(x)=2 x^{4} -6 x^{3} -4 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2 x^{4} -6 x^{3} -4 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x}) \\ & =2\cdot4x^{3}-6\cdot3x^{2}-4\cdot2x+x^{-2} \\ & =8 x^{3} -18 x^{2} -8 x + \frac{1}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(2) & =8 (2)^{3} -18 (2)^{2} -8 (2) + \frac{1}{(2)^{2}} \\ & =\frac{1}{4}-72-16+64 \\ & =-24+\frac{1}{4} \\ & =-\frac{95}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=2$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(2)=-\frac{95}{4}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3 x^{4} -7 x^{3} -6 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x}) \\ & =3\cdot4x^{3}-7\cdot3x^{2}-6\cdot2x+x^{-2} \\ & =12 x^{3} -21 x^{2} -12 x + \frac{1}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(3) & =12 (3)^{3} -21 (3)^{2} -12 (3) + \frac{1}{(3)^{2}} \\ & =\frac{1}{9}-189-36+324 \\ & =99+\frac{1}{9} \\ & =\frac{892}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=3$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(3)=\frac{892}{9}.
$$

Let $f(x)=3 x^{4} -7 x^{3} -6 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=4$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(4).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3 x^{4} -7 x^{3} -6 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x}) \\ & =3\cdot4x^{3}-7\cdot3x^{2}-6\cdot2x+x^{-2} \\ & =12 x^{3} -21 x^{2} -12 x + \frac{1}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=4$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(4) & =12 (4)^{3} -21 (4)^{2} -12 (4) + \frac{1}{(4)^{2}} \\ & =\frac{1}{16}-336-48+768 \\ & =384+\frac{1}{16} \\ & =\frac{6145}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=4$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(4)=\frac{6145}{16}.
$$
